My plot is very small, only a small piece of land here in Balaka, and maize is what feeds my family. I have no schooling and I do what my father did and what my neighbors do. If I get the coupon from the government this year, I will buy one bag of fertilizer and share it on my plot, but the plot is too small for a whole bag of NPK and a whole bag of urea, so I use little by little. I put the goat and chicken droppings I gather around the house on the plot before the rains, and I plant pigeon pea between the maize like my neighbors do. I cannot afford hybrid seed every year, so I keep some seed from last harvest and plant that. The rains here in Balaka are not strong, sometimes the dry spell comes and the maize suffers, but I have no way to bring water to the field — I just pray the rains come well.
